name: Bionic contact lens

card.summary: A bionic contact lens is an experimental lens with embedded electronics aimed at augmented-reality displays and sensors; it could add vision and eye-appearance features.
card.aka: Smart contact lens, AR contact lens
card.note: Experimental; no consumer product is established.

quick.overview:
A bionic contact lens embeds tiny circuits, LEDs, sensors and an antenna into a soft lens. The aim is overlays on the wearer's view and tear-fluid monitoring, built into an accessory worn on the eye.

Its link to looks is as a future eye accessory rather than a cosmetic effect today. A University of Washington prototype in 2008 had a one-pixel LED and was tested in rabbits.
quick.how: Not available as a consumer product; development is by research groups and companies.
quick.risks: Challenges include power, biocompatibility and oxygen permeability.

lead: A bionic contact lens is a thin, flexible lens that embeds microelectronics such as LEDs, circuits, sensors and antennas to display information or monitor the eye [3]. The concept was demonstrated in 2008 at the University of Washington under Babak Parviz, with a one-pixel red LED powered wirelessly and tested in rabbits for up to 20 minutes [3].

Companies including Mojo Vision and Innovega have pursued AR lens systems; Mojo pivoted in 2023 towards licensing microLED platforms [3]. Wikipedia calls the device a proposed one, with wireless power as an expected development [1].
No clinical studies of consumer use for appearance exist.

angle.text: Developers aim at displays and health sensing in an eye-worn device. Its connection to looks is as a prospective eye accessory.

paras: Components include microLED arrays, tear sensors for glucose or intraocular pressure, microprocessors and antennas for wireless power and data [3].
No studies found for appearance use. Early prototypes were safety tested in rabbits [1].

timeline.event: Mojo Vision pivots to microLED licensing [3].
